edges.description: Less repolarizing IKs adds to the action potential lengthening. Murine myocytes have little IKs, so this arm was not what lengthened the action potential in the study's own cells.
Lengthened ventricular action potentials are recorded clinically as QT prolongation.

When ventricular refractoriness outlasts the sinus cycle, every second atrial impulse reaches refractory ventricle and is not conducted, producing functional 2:1 block below the His bundle. The intermediate is prolonged ventricular refractoriness. Established in general long QT syndrome; the calmodulinopathy registry calls the block functional but no calmodulin study measured refractoriness.
At extreme action potential durations the rate dependence of repolarization differs across the ventricular wall, so repolarization alternates beat to beat.
RyR2 calcium leak produces delayed-afterdepolarization-triggered activity, the substrate of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.
Delayed repolarization predisposes to early afterdepolarizations and torsades de pointes, which can end in sudden cardiac death.
Syncopal episodes in CPVT are caused by fast bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.
Catecholaminergic ventricular tachycardia can degenerate into ventricular fibrillation.

Hypoxic-ischemic brain injury from cardiac arrest can cause seizures. The founding CALM2 D96V proband suffered a cerebral infarction after her first arrest and later developed seizures attributed to that injury.

Hypoxic-ischemic brain injury from cardiac arrest in early life can cause developmental delay. The founding CALM2 D96V proband had a cerebral infarction after her first arrest and later showed delays in every developmental domain.
Untreated ventricular fibrillation causes sudden death.
Exertion precipitates the ventricular arrhythmias. Emotional stress, the other adrenergic trigger reported, has no comparably specific ECTO term and is named only here.
Sinus bradycardia in heterozygous Calm2 N98S mice of both sexes.
edges.limitations: Mouse heart rate and pacemaker physiology differ from human; the human bradycardia is often fetal and accompanied by 2:1 block, which the model does not show.

nodes.description: A heterozygous missense variant in CALM2, usually de novo, alters a calmodulin calcium-binding EF-hand. The worked example is D133H, which changes a calcium-coordinating residue of the fourth EF-hand and destabilises calcium binding by the C-terminal lobe. Because CALM1, CALM2 and CALM3 encode an identical protein, the variant protein is one of six calmodulin alleles' products, yet it acts dominantly.

nodes.description: Calmodulin is an auxiliary subunit of the Kv7.1 (KCNQ1) channel that carries the repolarizing IKs current. CALM2 D133H weakens apo-calmodulin binding to the Kv7.1 helix B domain and reduces channel activation, limiting repolarizing potassium current. Shown for D133H in murine myocytes and peptide-binding assays; not established for other CALM2 variants.

nodes.description: Calmodulin bound to RyR2 normally inhibits sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release during diastole. CPVT-associated calmodulin variants fail to inhibit, or even activate, RyR2, producing calcium leak and a propensity to delayed-afterdepolarization-triggered activity. This is the mechanism of the CPVT and mixed CPVT/LQTS phenotypes of CALM2 carriers.
